detail.text: Distant Spread of Toxin Effect: effects may spread from the injection area to produce botulinum toxin effects; swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death

citations.quote: ## WARNING: Distant Spread of Toxin Effect

The effects of XEOMIN and all botulinum toxin products may spread from the area of injection to produce symptoms consistent with botulinum toxin effects. These symptoms have been reported hours to weeks after injection. Swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death.

detail.text: REMS required to ensure benefits outweigh risk of distant spread of toxin and potential medication errors from lack of interchangeability; consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for assessments

citations.quote: In accordance with 505-1 of the FDA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin after local injection, and the potential for medication errors related to the lack of interchangeability of Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) with other licensed botulinum toxin products.
The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

summary.text: Standard BLA under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act, received July 2, 2009 and approved July 30, 2010 without advisory committee referral; approval required a REMS and included postmarketing requirements and commitments.

citations.quote: Please refer to Biologics License Application (BLA) dated July 1, 2009, received July 2, 2009, submitted by Merz Pharmaceuticals under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) Injection.

Your application for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this biologic is not the first in its class, and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for these indications.

In accordance with 505-1 of the FDA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin after local injection, and the potential for medication errors related to the lack of interchangeability of Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) with other licensed botulinum toxin products.
